subject: Arcturus5b: elevated 5xx/timeout activity — interim customer comms & next steps
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: [ALERT] Arcturus5b uptick in 5xx on v2-small-route

Marcus / Ben —

Ops flagged a sustained spike in 5xx and request timeouts for model arcturus5b serving on v2-small-route starting ~08:48 PST. Error ratio climbed to ~6.7% over the 5m window (baseline ~0.3%). Initial triage shows majority of failures are 504/timeout from the runtime layer with a small subset 502 at the gateway.

Quick notes from the trace sampling:
- Latency tails grew; KV cache miss rate increased for requests with longer prompt prefixes.
- One GPU host (gw-rt-07) returned repeated late responses prior to connection reset.
- Autoscaler did not spawn additional capacity due to an intermittent metrics lag.

I'm creating a short bridge and will start collecting error samples + qps buckets. Recommend we prepare an external note for any affected customers likely to see degraded quality.

-- Neha
Senior Site Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: arcturus5b-error-samples-20261123.txt]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, support@fjordanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Arcturus5b — brief notice: transient elevated errors

James —

I wanted to proactively let you know we observed an elevated rate of 5xx/timeouts impacting the Arcturus5b model on the v2-small serving path this morning (started ~08:48 PST). Your account saw a subset of requests affected — we estimate roughly 4–8% of calls during the spike window based on our telemetry.

What we’ve done so far:
- Isolated the pattern to arcturus5b on v2-small-route; rolled traffic away from one host showing repeated late responses.
- Temporarily increased the region fallback pool and enabled quicker scaling for the affected route.
- Preserved error samples and request ids for your team and ours for root-cause analysis.

Immediate impact to you: you may have seen intermittent timeouts or delayed responses for a small percentage of completions. We do not believe outputs were corrupted — errors manifested as 504/timeouts or gateway 502s.

Next steps (we will):
- Continue collecting logs and traces; share redacted samples where useful.
- Follow up with a timeline and a short post-incident note once we have the root cause.
- Offer a credit for any failed requests above your normal baseline; Ben from your account team will follow up with details.

If you saw a specific failure pattern or have request ids, reply inline and we’ll prioritize. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll keep you updated.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

- Fallback: routing to arcturus5b-v1 is possible and safe; v1 has a slightly higher cost but stable behavior for your workload. If you want us to switch traffic for the nightly job window tonight, Ben can coordinate — we can do a targeted rule for your tenant.

Ben — can you confirm the account-level fallback and provide contact for scheduling the switch? Neha will continue deeper traces and a host-level analysis to determine root cause and whether a kernel/quantization path contributed to the failure.

Regards,

Subject: Arcturus5b — post-incident summary and next steps

James —

Following our investigation, attached is a short post-incident summary and next steps. High-level findings:
- Root cause: an edge case in the KV-cache interaction for long-prefix requests combined with a metrics emission race that delayed autoscaler reactions. The combination allowed a small set of hosts to accumulate elevated pending work and produce timeouts.
- Impact window: 2026-11-23 08:48–10:17 PST. Your account observed ~5% error rate in that window; we identified the three request ids you provided in our samples.
- Mitigations implemented: host restart for gw-rt-07, targeted routing to arcturus5b-v1 for your nightly job, tightened autoscaler metrics window, and a temporary increase in prefix cache warmup.

Planned permanent fixes and timeline:
- Patch to ensure autoscaler observes metrics emission on host-level (target: 2 weeks).
- KV-cache guardrails to drop stale entries gracefully (target: 3 weeks).
- Add regression checks to eval harness for long-prefix tail cases (target: 4 weeks).

We’ve applied a one-time account credit to cover retries outside your baseline; Ben is sending the billing note separately. A draft postmortem is on the shared drive (link below) — we welcome any questions.

Link: https://drive.redwood/reports/arcturus5b-interim-comm-20261123
Jira: JIRA-OPS-12987

Again, I’m sorry for the disruption. If you’d like a short call to walk through the findings and the remediation plan, I’m happy to schedule.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
